decisive_items: abdominal pain that began around the umbilicus 2 days earlier and migrated to the right lower quadrant
Ultrasound assessment was interpreted as compatible with plastron appendicitis

Computed tomography of the abdomen revealed a linear lesion within the intestinal lumen in the right lower quadrant, causing partial luminal obliteration and edema on the anterolateral aspect of the cecum
response.rationale: Migratory pain, leukocytosis, and imaging (ultrasound suggesting plastron appendicitis, CT showing cecal edema and luminal obliteration) strongly support appendicitis. Intussusception is less likely in adults and lacks typical imaging features; gastroenteritis is contradicted by denied diarrhea/vomiting and focal findings.

rejected.why: Denied diarrhea, nausea, vomiting; focal right lower quadrant findings and imaging favor appendicitis, not gastroenteritis.
CT linear lesion could suggest intussusception, but ultrasound interpretation and clinical migration point to appendicitis; adult intussusception is uncommon and less supported.
